edition.authority: Council of Florence under Eugene IV
edition.notes: A catalog-level identification of the conventional received Latin text of the doctrinal sections. The bull was promulgated in parallel Latin and Greek; only the Latin as received in Denzinger is identified here, and no claim is made about the Greek wording. No exact artifact of a printed Denzinger edition is retained or hashed. The 1439 conciliar act is public domain; particular printed editions of Denzinger retain their own editorial rights.
edition.publication: Latin text of the bull as printed in Denzinger's Enchiridion symbolorum, nn. 1300-1308 (older numbering 691-694)
edition.title: Laetentur caeli — Latin text as received in Denzinger's Enchiridion symbolorum

alternate_titles: Bull of union with the Greeks
work.author: Council of Florence under Eugene IV
work.description: The bull of union with the Greek Church promulgated at the Council of Florence on 6 July 1439, defining the procession of the Holy Spirit from the Father and the Son, the legitimacy of the Filioque addition, the validity of both leavened and unleavened bread, the lot of the departed (purgatory; the purified received at once into heaven and seeing clearly God himself three and one as he is, yet according to the diversity of merits one more perfectly than another; the immediate descent of those dying in mortal or original sin), and the primacy of the Roman Pontiff. It was subscribed at Florence and afterwards repudiated at Constantinople; its doctrinal force in the Catholic Church does not depend on its reception in the East.
work.title: Laetentur caeli
